title: Causal Agency: A Persistence–Control Theory of Adaptive Systems

equations.label: Def-1
equations.meaning: System state evolution: the state x evolves according to a dynamical rule F, and C denotes the constraint structure influencing that evolution. Basis of Definition 1 (a constrained dynamical system). Also introduced informally in 5.3 and restated in Appendix B.

equations.label: Def-2
equations.text: x(t) ∈ V,  where V ⊆ S is the viable region of the state space S, for all times in the interval of observation
equations.meaning: A system exhibits persistence over an interval if its trajectory remains within the viable region V of state space compatible with continued existence/functioning. Basis of Definition 2 (persistence). Also introduced in 5.2 and restated in Appendix B.

equations.label: Persistence-Regulation-Condition
equations.text: d/dt [ d(x(t), V) ] < 0  (in expectation), where d(x,V) is the distance between state x and the viable region V
equations.meaning: Persistence regulation occurs when system dynamics tend to decrease, in expectation, the distance between the system state and the viable region — stabilizing trajectories without necessarily altering the constraint structure.

equations.label: Constraint-Evolution
equations.meaning: Base form of constraint dynamics: the future constraint structure depends on the current system state and the existing configuration of constraints, allowing the constraint structure itself to evolve as a function of system activity. Restated in 8.1 and Appendix B/C.
equations.paper_tier: definition (schematic representation, not yet the agency condition)

equations.label: State-Constraint-Coupling
equations.meaning: State–constraint coupling: the constraint structure's evolution genuinely depends on system state. Necessary but explicitly stated as not sufficient for agency.
equations.paper_tier: definition (necessary condition, part of the agency criterion)

equations.label: Def-3 (Agency-Condition)
equations.text: ∂Tp/∂C · ∂C/∂x > 0,  where Tp is the expected persistence time of the system within the viable region V
equations.meaning: A system exhibits agency when system-induced constraint changes increase the expected persistence duration of the system. Basis of Definition 3 (agency as constraint regulation oriented toward persistence). Restated in Appendix B and Appendix C (Causal Structure of Agency Emergence).

equations.label: Proto-Agency-Condition
equations.section: 8.2–8.3 Level 0 / Level 1; 9.2 Control Systems and Proto-Agency
equations.meaning: Systems with zero state-constraint coupling: Level 0 (passive persistence, no regulation at all) or Level 1/proto-agency (persistence regulation present via feedback/homeostasis, but no modification of the constraint structure itself). Also used in Appendix B to define proto-agency.

equations.label: L3-Constraint-Evolution-History
equations.section: 8.5 Level 3: Adaptive Constraint Regulation / 9.3 Learning Systems and Adaptive Agency
equations.text: C_{t+1} = G(x_t, C_t, H_t),  where H_t is the system's interaction history
equations.meaning: Constraint evolution becomes history-dependent: learning mechanisms alter internal parameters/policies based on accumulated experience, making constraint modulation flexible and history-dependent (Level 3 of the agency hierarchy).

equations.label: L4-Constraint-Evolution-Predictive
equations.section: 8.6 Level 4: Predictive Constraint Regulation / 9.4 Predictive Artificial Agents
equations.text: C_{t+1} = G(x_t, C_t, x̂_{t+k}),  where x̂_{t+k} represents predicted future states
equations.meaning: Constraint regulation becomes forward-looking: systems with predictive/internal models regulate constraints in anticipation of future states over longer temporal horizons (Level 4 of the agency hierarchy).

equations.label: L5-Meta-Regulation
equations.section: 8.7 Level 5: Reflective Constraint Regulation / 9.6 Toward Strong Artificial Agency
equations.meaning: Meta-regulation: the system modifies the rule G governing its own constraint-modulation dynamics, i.e. it can revise the strategies/policies through which it regulates persistence (Level 5, reflective agency — the highest level of the hierarchy).
